warning.author: Various Chinese storytellers; collected and retold in English by J. Macgowan
warning.locator: THE REWARD OF A BENEVOLENT LIFE; THE REWARD OF A BENEVOLENT LIFE, normalized characters 2737-3601
warning.excerpt: Before very long a great flood will take place in this district, and will sweep everything before it. It will be so sudden that men will not be able to take measures to preserve either their lives or their property--so instantaneous will be the rush of the mighty streams, like ocean floods, from the mountains you can see in the West. My advice to you is to commence at once the construction of boats to carry you and your most precious effects away. When the news first comes that the waters are rising, have them anchored in the creek that flows close by your doors; and when the crisis arrives, delay not a moment, but hurry on board and fly for your lives." "But when will that be?" asked Chung anxiously. "I may not tell you the precise day or hour," replied the bonze; "but when the eyes of the stone lions in the East Street of the city shed tears of blood
warning.note: Quotation from J. Macgowan's English literary collection of folktales; distinguish this written version from a community-wide canon.

rescue.author: Various Chinese storytellers; collected and retold in English by J. Macgowan
rescue.locator: THE REWARD OF A BENEVOLENT LIFE; THE REWARD OF A BENEVOLENT LIFE, normalized characters 9322-9806
rescue.excerpt: Chung replied that at such a time, when a human being was in extreme danger of being drowned, personal interests ought not to be considered at all. He had faithfully obeyed the command of the priest in saving animal life, but how much more valuable was a man than any of the lower orders of creation? "Whatever may happen," he said, "I cannot let this man drown before my eyes," and as the boat just then came alongside the swimmer, he was hauled into it and delivered from his peril.
rescue.note: Quotation from J. Macgowan's English literary collection of folktales; distinguish this written version from a community-wide canon.

narrativeBlocks.title: A warning with a sign
narrativeBlocks.body: In Macgowan's collected literary tale, a priest warns Chung's household about a sudden flood and tells them to leave when the stone lions' eyes appear to shed blood.

narrativeBlocks.title: The warning and the signal
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from the cited English edition (whitespace normalized): “Before very long a great flood will take place in this district, and will sweep everything before it. narrativeBlocks.title: Chung chooses to rescue
narrativeBlocks.body: When the flood arrives, Chung's wife recalls the warning not to rescue a man from the river. Chung decides that a person in immediate danger must still be saved.

narrativeBlocks.title: A collected tale, not a social survey
narrativeBlocks.body: Macgowan's Chinese Folk-Lore Tales is a literary collection in English. This episode supports claims about this written tale, not a universal Chinese belief or historical flood event.

narrativeBlocks.title: The title's moral is tested
narrativeBlocks.body: The story tests benevolence through a conflict between a supernatural warning and the immediate duty Chung feels toward a drowning stranger.
